newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil- high sulphur down, tightness overdone.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil- high sulphur down, tightness overdone.

text.p: Physical fuel oil trading was very slow on Tuesday with traders looking to an equally quiet swaps market for indications on prices.
High sulphur cracked cargoes consoliated at the lower levels that were done Friday.
"I see the market in the high $90s, not at the $104 that we saw last week," said one trader. A U.K utlity bought on Friday at $99 cif NWE for a September 1-15 delivery.
The market was expected to receive a boost from Portugal's EdP tendering for six cargoes of high sulphur cracked for September with an option for a further two cargoes for October.
The tender should be awarded by the end of the week, traders said. Swaps in the Med gained 50-75 cents on the news.
Supplies remain tight, but not as tight as previously thought and fresh Russian availabilities will ease the situation, dealers said.

Low sulphur cracked material was particuarly quiet on the wet side although 80-90,000 tonnes was required by a Portuguese buyer for first half September delivery. Dealers said prices were being talked a slight premium to the paper market of $106-106.50 fob NWE. The buyer was expected to use own tonnage.
